   AI is increasingly providing health guidance, with over 300 million weekly inquiries to ChatGPT about health. However, the article discusses the ethical implications of AI's influence on behavior and the need for safety evaluations that consider long-term harms, not just immediate dangers. The federal government is looking to integrate AI more deeply into medical care, which raises questions about the balance between doing no harm and promoting good.

2. **Why is Nvidia so powerful in the AI world, and what could Jensen Huang’s scandal really cost?**  
   Nvidia's dominance in the AI sector is attributed to its graphic processing units (GPUs), which are essential for AI model training. Despite competition from companies like Google and AMD, Nvidia remains unchallenged in speed and efficiency. The article also touches on the geopolitical implications of AI chip production, particularly in the context of US-China relations.  
   [Read more here](https://theconversation.com/why-is-nvidia-so-powerful-in-the-ai-world-and-what-could-jensen-huangs-scandal-really-cost-296257).

items.title: Why is Nvidia so powerful in the AI world, and what could Jensen Huang’s scandal really cost?
items.summary:
The AI sector is notorious for the amount of circular financing going on – where companies invest in their own suppliers or customers. Nvidia is a key player in this loop.

Investors are already fretting over whether the enormous amounts of money sunk into AI can ever return profits.

While leading AI model builders Anthropic and OpenAI are moving toward public listings or fresh funding rounds, both face harsh reality checks. [...] The now multi-trillion-dollar company got its start making chips called graphic processing units (GPUs), used largely for video games. However, these chips – and their successors – turned out to be ideal for the kind of number-crunching needed for training and using AI models.

Other companies such as Google and AMD have tried to make chips that can compete with Nvidia for speed and efficiency, however neither has been able to displace Nvidia from its dominance of the AI market. [...] Computer chips – specifically the chips used to produce and run artificial intelligence (AI) systems – have become a key front in the United States’ rivalry with China for geopolitical power and influence. The most powerful chips are needed for the most advanced AI, and the US has tried to maintain its edge over China by restricting access to those chips.

While the Chinese government rejects claims of espionage, Alice Huang has reportedly been under investigation by the US for years.

items.summary:
One theory about an AI Armageddon doesn't involve robots who look like Arnold Schwarzenegger hunting us down with laser guns. AI could just take over our natural habitat, as we've done with other animals and plants, which would leave us without food and shelter.

Here's a thought exercise: If AI were evaluating whether humans were worth saving for conservation purposes, would we grade out more as an invasive species or one that made important contributions to the ecosystem? [...] # Someone drained my bank account. Then the real nightmare began | Opinion

## Over time, AI is going to turn our brains to mush. People won't be able to remember phone numbers, basic grammar or directions to places they've visited once or twice without consulting AI overlords.

Portrait of Blake Fontenay

There's an old episode of "The Simpsons" where Homer, the TV show's booze-addled antihero, offers a hilarious toast: "To alcohol! The cause of – and solution to – all of life's problems." [...] People – some of us, at least – are worried about AI eventually overthrowing human civilization. Even more immediately, there's widespread concern about the proliferation of data centers needed to support AI operations.

Yet at the same time we're collectively wringing our hands about those issues, we are meekly surrendering more and more control to machines over our everyday lives.

Here are some recent articles discussing how AI labs are optimizing training costs:

1. **DeepSeek's Efficiency Breakthroughs**  
   DeepSeek, a Chinese AI company, has made significant strides in reducing training costs through its mixture of experts (MoE) architecture, hardware optimization, model distillation, and reinforcement learning. This approach allows the model to use only the necessary portions for specific tasks, drastically lowering compute resource requirements. Additionally, DeepSeek's models are optimized to run efficiently on less powerful and cheaper GPUs. This innovation has positioned DeepSeek as a competitive player in the AI industry.  
   [Read more here](https://www.bgr.com/2304275/who-owns-deepseek-ai).

2. **Energy Disparities in Generative AI**  
   Research indicates that generative AI consumes significantly more energy when processing non-English text, with costs ranging from 1.4 to 180 times higher. To address this, experts suggest that AI developers should create resources tailored for various languages and consider using translation pipelines to improve efficiency. This could help reduce the barriers for non-English speakers in accessing AI technologies.  
   [Read more here](https://news.engin.umich.edu/2026/11/generative-ai-uses-more-energy-on-non-english-text).

3. **Israeli Startups Innovating in AI Cost Reduction**  
   Israeli companies are exploring ways to reduce the enormous computing power and costs associated with training and running AI models. These startups are leveraging innovative technologies to compete with established foreign rivals, aiming to make AI more affordable and accessible.  
   [Read more here](https://www.haaretz.com/israel-news/tech-news/2026-11-05/ty-article/.premium/can-these-israeli-companies-make-ai-cheaper-and-faster-with-the-help-of-ai/000001a1-a62d-d0e2-a5e3-a7effe5c0000).

items.title: Generative AI uses more energy on non-English text
items.summary:
“AI developers should be creating more resources for those languages with an energy and cost disparity,” said Rada Mihalcea, the Janice M. Jenkins Collegiate Professor of Computer Science and Engineering, director of the U-M AI Lab and corresponding author of the study. “Crowdsourcing native speakers to help translate material or create resources to get enough training data could also help improve efficiency.” [...] To help fix the cost disparity, the researchers recommend that companies optimize their services for more languages. This could entail routing user queries to models tailored to specific languages. Companies could also translate user prompts to English before feeding them to a more generalized model, provided the translation is reliable. [...] ## Key takeaways

   Gen AI uses 1.4 to 180 times more energy to produce text outside the English language.
   Higher energy costs increase the barrier to using AI for billions of people worldwide—they must either pay more or switch to a non-native language.
   AI developers could improve energy efficiency by training models optimized for specific languages or incorporating translation pipelines into their services.

items.summary: The Computational Photonics and AI Design Lab at Hanyang University, led by Prof. Haejun Chung, develops optical and electromagnetic devices through large-scale simulation, inverse design, and artificial intelligence. Its methods include adjoint optimization, physics-guided neural operators, and diffusion-based generative models. Research topics span metasurfaces, visible and thermal-imaging metalenses, CMOS image-sensor color routers, augmented-reality waveguide couplers, integrated photonics, [...] Neural-network-based methods provide response and field surrogates, candidate-generation models, and learned components within iterative solvers. Physics-informed learning and neural operators are examined alongside tandem and generative inverse-design networks. Their computational benefit depends on data-generation and training costs, repeated use, and prediction accuracy within the validated domain. [...] The Smart Optics Lab at Korea University Sejong Campus, led by Prof. Sunae So in the Department of Electro-Mechanical Systems Engineering, studies nanophotonics and AI-assisted inverse design. Its research covers metasurface holography, augmented-reality optics, medical visualization, radiative cooling, and surface-enhanced Raman scattering sensing. The group combines FDTD and rigorous coupled-wave analysis, deep-learning surrogates, and adjoint-based topology optimization with fabrication

Dưới đây là 5 ý chính từ bài viết trên trang OpenAI về nghiên cứu:

1. **Mục tiêu nghiên cứu**: OpenAI tập trung vào việc phát triển trí tuệ nhân tạo tổng quát (AGI) với mục tiêu đảm bảo rằng AGI sẽ mang lại lợi ích cho toàn nhân loại.

2. **Các lĩnh vực nghiên cứu**: OpenAI tiến hành nghiên cứu trong các lĩnh vực như mô hình tiên tiến, lý luận, hệ thống đa phương thức và triển khai an toàn.

3. **Mô hình GPT**: Dòng mô hình GPT của OpenAI được thiết kế để hiểu ngữ cảnh, tạo nội dung và lý luận qua văn bản, hình ảnh và nhiều hơn nữa. Các mô hình này nhanh chóng, linh hoạt và tiết kiệm chi phí.

4. **Nghiên cứu về hình ảnh và âm thanh**: OpenAI đã đạt được những tiến bộ trong việc tạo ra hình ảnh, hiểu ngôn ngữ hình ảnh và phát triển các mô hình có khả năng nhận diện và tạo ra âm thanh, bao gồm nhận diện giọng nói và tạo ra cuộc trò chuyện tự nhiên.

5. **Tìm kiếm nhân tài**: OpenAI đang tích cực tìm kiếm những cá nhân tài năng để gia nhập đội ngũ nghiên cứu của mình, nhằm thúc đẩy sự phát triển của AI.

Bạn có thể xem chi tiết bài viết tại [đây](https://openai.com/research/).
